meta.title: Raising prices in 2027 while churn is rising
meta.subtitle: Discussion document for the CEO and leadership team, 2027 pricing decision
meta.purpose: Decide whether and how to raise prices in 2027
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data; every number from the briefing pack

inputs.label: Checkpoint choices made on the user's behalf (user unavailable)
inputs.content: Mode deck_detailed; audience CEO and leadership team deciding the 2027 plan; theme navy; storyline built as drafted; no placeholders left

storyline.governing_thought: Raise 2027 prices in mid-market and enterprise, stage SMB behind a stop rule, spare promotion customers

exec_summary.text: Churn is rising because of the 2025 promotion, not core price resistance

sub_points.text: The promotion cohort drives about 94% of the SMB rise
Onboarding alone removes about a tenth of SMB churn

exec_summary.text: Pricing power sits in mid-market and enterprise, not yet in SMB

sub_points.text: Inkwell's $9 plan undercuts our $15; win rate fell to 38%

exec_summary.text: The CFO's 12% plan is worth about $7.6M in 2027, not $10.3M

sub_points.text: Renewal dates and 7% enterprise caps cut the gain
A segmented plan keeps most of it, with less risk

exec_summary.text: A segmented plan adds about $5.6M and meets the 15% goal, with no cushion

sub_points.text: The 8% SMB step nets only about $0.7M
Mid-market and enterprise move in January; SMB waits for a test

next_steps.action: Approve the segmented 2027 price plan and its stop rules
Pull H2 2026 SMB churn by cohort to confirm the discount cliff has passed
Set up the randomized SMB renewal test and the promotion-cohort activation drive
Check which multi-year enterprise contracts allow a 2027 escalator before renewal
Define the board dashboard's churn measure and restate it by segment

constraints.effect: existing customers plus the plan reach about 15.0%, level with the objective and with no cushion; titles and exec item 4 say 'no cushion'

constraints.item: Keep overall net revenue retention above 100%
constraints.effect: about 115% with the plan; not the binding constraint

constraints.item: Price changes only at renewal: 85% of mid-market and 40% of enterprise ARR renews in 2027
constraints.effect: cuts the CFO's $10.3M to $7.6M and sizes our plan on renewing ARR only

constraints.item: 60% of enterprise ARR capped at 7% a year

constraints.effect: SMB step shown net of a 2023-like response ($0.7M, not $1.3M); mid-market response not modelled because the only test was on new sign-ups, so the ARR title says 'no cushion' and a mid-market stop level is set

constraints.item: Possible enterprise escalators before renewal ('enterprise contracts follow their own terms')
constraints.effect: upside of up to about $1.0M left out; a next step checks the contracts

constraints.item: Inkwell's $9 plan and the falling SMB win rate
constraints.effect: new SMB sign-ups stay at $15; win rate is a guardrail

alternatives.option: Mid-market and enterprise only; hold all SMB prices in 2027
alternatives.why: safest, but about $0.7M short of the 15% objective before new customers; it becomes the fallback if the SMB stop rule triggers

alternatives.option: Hold all prices, as the CEO's caution implies
alternatives.why: the churn rise sits in the promotion cohort; holding mid-market and enterprise gives up about $4.3M where retention is strongest

alternatives.option: CFO: 12% on every plan from January
alternatives.why: worth $7.6M, not $10.3M, with a third resting on SMB and the promotion cohort

alternatives.option: Mid-market and uncapped enterprise at 12% instead of 10%
alternatives.why: adds about $0.7M gross but goes beyond the only tested level, and mid-market churn has edged up

failure_threshold.driver: mid-market churn response at renewal to the 10% step
failure_threshold.threshold: the step stops paying if mid-market monthly churn rises above about 1.6% (0.8% + 0.76 percentage points); the 15% objective slips with any material mid-market loss because the plan only matches it
failure_threshold.range: end-2027 ARR before new customers: low $98.25M (SMB step stopped) / base $98.9M / high $99.6M (no SMB churn response)

consistency.headline: Palisade should raise 2027 prices in mid-market and enterprise, stage SMB behind a stop rule and spare the 2025 promotion customers
consistency.fix: after the audit the ARR claim reads 'level with the objective, with no cushion' rather than 'above it', and the SMB step is shown net of churn

sections.title: The segmented plan and its rollout

lead_message.text: The churn rise is an SMB problem: mid-market rose slightly and enterprise did not move

slides.rationale: Two periods across three segments -> clustered columns
slides.unit_line: **Monthly logo churn by segment**, % of customers, H1 2025 and H1 2026

sidebar.header: The rise is concentrated in the self-serve segment
sidebar.caption: relative rise in SMB monthly logo churn in a year
bullets: **SMB:** holds most of the customers but less than a quarter of ARR, and carries almost all of the rise
**Mid-market:** a small rise from a low base, with no exit reasons in the pack; worth watching at renewal
**Enterprise:** unchanged, held in place by multi-year contracts

footnotes: The board dashboard's "monthly churn 1.4% → 2.3%" has no definition and matches neither a customer- nor an ARR-weighted average of these segments (see backup)

lead_message.text: The 2025 promotion cohort drives about 94% of the SMB churn rise; other SMB customers barely moved

slides.rationale: What adds up to the rise -> waterfall

**Other SMB:** up a tenth of a percentage point, despite Inkwell

footnotes: Each group is weighted by its mid-2026 customer count (3,800 not from the promotion, 2,100 from it); the cohort's rate is implied from Table 1, not reported
The cohort is compared with the 2.0% monthly churn of similar SMB customers in H1 2025

lead_message.text: Promotion customers never got started and left when the discount ended, while other customers' price complaints held steady

slides.rationale: Two clauses, one claim about the cohort -> two panels, no arrow

slides.so_what: The cohort reacted to its price doubling; a list-price rise on top would hit the group likeliest to leave
footnotes: Most promotion-cohort customers who left did so within two months of the discount ending; the promotion gave 50% off for the first six months, February to August 2025
SMB customers who send fewer than five documents in their first month churn at about three times the rate of those who send more

lead_message.text: Onboarding alone can remove about a tenth of SMB churn; most of the promotion's damage was a one-off discount cliff
highlights: If the cohort also gets started

**Onboarding:** a 72% start rate, as in other cohorts, removes the rest of the cohort's excess
**Floor:** SMB churn then sits at the rate of customers not from the promotion

lead_message.text: Our own price history says mid-market barely reacts to a rise and SMB churn recovers within six months

body.assumptions_header: The step is small and close to break-even, so it needs a stop rule
assumptions: Break-even: the step stops paying if it lifts monthly SMB churn by more than about 0.6 percentage points through 2027 (8% ÷ 108% ÷ 12 months)
Customers not from the promotion react as all SMB did in 2023; Inkwell's $9 plan did not exist then, so the response could be larger
Lost customers are valued at the new price; any effect on new-customer win rates is not included
The promotion cohort is left out of the step

footnotes: Estimate by the team from the briefing pack; the live formula is in the Calculations sheet of the source workbook
